summary: Acceptance plan for warehouse order allocation and inventory reservation based on stakeholder interviews.

requirements.description: Reserve all lines of an order together atomically after aggregating repeated SKUs. If any SKU is missing or has insufficient stock, reject without deducting any stock.

sources.quote: Reserve all lines of an order together or reserve nothing; repeated SKU lines must be added together before checking stock.

acceptance.given: An initial inventory stock and order lines containing single or repeated SKUs.
acceptance.then: Either all aggregated quantities are subtracted atomically or no stock is consumed and insufficient_stock is returned.

requirements.description: Allocate inventory to expedited orders ahead of normal orders while preserving arrival order within each priority tier.

sources.quote: Expedited orders get stock before normal orders; preserve arrival order within each priority.

acceptance.given: A list of orders with expedited and normal priorities competing for stock.
acceptance.then: All valid expedited orders are fulfilled before normal orders, maintaining arrival order within each tier.

requirements.description: Treat order IDs idempotently by processing only the first occurrence and ignoring subsequent duplicate IDs completely.

sources.quote: An order ID is idempotent: process only its first occurrence and ignore later duplicates.

acceptance.given: An order list containing duplicate occurrences of order IDs.
acceptance.when: Order validation and fulfillment is executed.
acceptance.then: The first occurrence claims the ID and later occurrences are entirely ignored.

requirements.description: Reject invalid lines or orders without modifying inventory stock, preserving caller input immutability.

sources.quote: Invalid order lines must be rejected without changing stock, and callers must retain their original input objects.

acceptance.given: Stock and order inputs passed to allocation functions.
acceptance.when: Validation encounters invalid lines, invalid orders, or safe-integer overflow.
acceptance.then: The rejection reason is recorded, stock remains unchanged, and input arguments are not mutated.

assumptions: Stock levels are nonnegative safe integers and line quantities are positive safe integers.
Orders with invalid priority are rejected as invalid_order and still claim their ID against duplicate occurrences.
Invalid or missing order IDs produce rejections with id null and reason invalid_order without claiming an ID.
Caller input objects and arrays are never mutated.
